content:
The Punjab Grade 9 Physics smart syllabus is included in the 6 November 2026 PECTAA notification for academic session 2026-27 and the annual examination 2027. This guide explains how to use the subject section, with a subject-only PDF rather than an unrelated multi-subject download.

[Open the Physics PDF resource, preview and download](/smart-syllabus/grade-9/physics/). The attachment on this article also opens the same subject document.

## What does this subject's ALP change?

The opening exclusion table identifies selected parts of Physical Quantities and Measurements, Kinematics, Dynamics and Turning Effects of Force. Examples include mass-measuring instruments, time-measuring instruments, measurement errors, uncertainty, precision and accuracy in Chapter 1. These are topic-level entries, not an instruction to discard every measurement concept.

In Kinematics the table names types of motion and the gradients of distance-time and speed-time graphs. In Dynamics it identifies fundamental forces, forces in a free-body diagram, limitations of Newton's laws and mechanical/electronic balances. Chapter 4 includes centre of gravity and centre of mass, selected stability material and the comparison of rotational and translational motion.

The exercise column separately identifies MCQs, short answers, constructed responses, comprehensive questions and numerical problems. A revised reference appears in the Dynamics constructed-response row. These examples come from the first subject page; the remaining pages contain further instructions and assessment material. Read the complete eight-page subject PDF before preparing a final checklist.

The details above highlight identifiable entries and preparation instructions. They are not presented as a replacement for every row of the original document. Where a table continues across pages, read the continuation before deciding whether a topic or question remains in scope.

The image preserves the covering notification. The downloadable file is an extract of the subject pages; the complete official booklet remains linked under Sources. The extracted PDF does not include unrelated subjects and has not been rewritten as a substitute notification.

## How should you mark your textbook?

Work with the approved textbook edition for this session. First locate the chapter or unit name, then the subsection, page number and exercise reference. Keep separate marks for excluded topics and excluded questions. A row that removes a particular example is narrower than a row that removes an entire exercise; neither should be expanded without evidence.

Make a retained-work checklist after completing the exclusions. This is more useful for daily revision than a list of crossed-out pages alone. If your edition has different pagination, match the wording and ask your teacher to reconcile the difference. Do not silently transfer a page range from another grade or academic year.

### Build a numerical checklist, not just a formula sheet

For each retained numerical problem, write the known quantities, the unknown quantity and the physical relationship linking them. Convert units before substitution and keep the unit with the final answer. Then explain whether the result is physically plausible. This separates a calculation you understand from one whose answer you memorised.

A deletion in a measurement subsection does not make all measurement skills irrelevant. A retained force or energy question may still require units and interpretation. Learn the prerequisites needed to solve retained work, while keeping the officially excluded assessment references distinct. Your teacher can help with a prerequisite that is no longer directly assessed.

### Keep conceptual and calculation practice separate

Use one notebook column for why a relationship holds and another for how to calculate with it. Draw the physical situation before choosing an equation. If your result has the wrong sign, revisit the chosen direction; if its size is unreasonable, revisit conversion and substitution. These checks are useful even when the final answer happens to match.

When practising a retained explanation, answer the actual command: define, distinguish, explain or derive. A definition alone is not a derivation. For diagrams, label quantities consistently with your written working. Choose practice from retained material only after checking all columns of the ALP table.

### Review mistakes by cause

Record whether each mistake came from a wrong concept, wrong equation, algebra, units or incomplete explanation. Redo the question without looking at the correction. On a later day, attempt a similar retained question with different values. The aim is to reproduce the reasoning, not the appearance of a solved example.

## What does the assessment material help you practise?

The subject section includes the instructions and assessment material that follow its syllabus notice. Read the objective and subjective instructions separately. Check the number of questions offered, the number required, the marks for each part and the available time. Copy these into a practice plan before starting a timed attempt.

Use the model paper to learn the format and expected level of response. It is not a leak, a guess paper or a guarantee that those same questions will appear. Retained material remains important even if a particular example does not appear in the model. Where a teacher provides an additional practice paper, compare its scope with this current document first.

![Assessment or continuation page from the Grade 9 Physics subject section](/images/smart-syllabus/2027/grade-9-physics-paper.webp)

This second image comes from within this subject section. Open the PDF for the surrounding pages and full-size text; an image viewed on a small phone is not a practical replacement for the downloadable document.

## A practical revision cycle for this subject

Begin with one retained unit or manageable group of questions. Read it, close the book and attempt a short recall task. Review the difference between your answer and the required explanation or method. Record the specific weakness, then return to it after a gap. This makes revision measurable without pretending that simply rereading a chapter proves understanding.

Before a timed paper, check your retained-work list for gaps. During the attempt, follow the stated choices and number each answer clearly. Afterwards, separate knowledge errors from presentation or timing errors. Plan the next study block around the weakest category rather than repeating only the questions you already answer comfortably.

Keep notes and past papers useful but subordinate to the current syllabus. An older paper may contain content that is now excluded. Filter such practice deliberately; do not assume an old question is in scope just because it appeared in a board examination before.

### Is this the full textbook or only the subject syllabus?

It is the 8-page Physics subject section extracted from the Grade 9 notification booklet. It contains the syllabus notice and accompanying assessment material, not the full textbook. The official multi-subject booklet is available through the source link below.

### Does smart syllabus mean I can skip every chapter mentioned?

No. Read the level of the exclusion: a topic, example, exercise, question or subpart. A chapter can contain both retained and excluded material. The exact table wording matters more than a shortened list shared without its page and exercise references.

### Can I preview the PDF on my phone?

Use Preview document in the attached-document block. If your browser does not display an embedded PDF comfortably, use Open document or Download PDF. Keep the saved copy available for revision, and zoom the original pages when checking small references or Urdu text.

### Does this notice announce my examination date?

A syllabus notification and an examination date sheet are different documents. This booklet concerns scope and assessment guidance for the stated session and annual examination. Check your board's separate date sheet and any later amendments for the examination schedule.

### What if a later notice changes this document?

A later applicable official amendment may change the preparation instructions. Check the issuing authority and your board before the examination, and compare notification dates and reference numbers. If a circulating image differs from the original booklet, use the complete official notice to investigate the difference.

Mark errors such as an incorrect charge, symbol, coefficient or condition, then rewrite the answer correctly. Use retained question types from the official model paper to check presentation under time pressure.

## What does the assessment material help you practise?

The subject section includes the instructions and assessment material that follow its syllabus notice. Read the objective and subjective instructions separately. Check the number of questions offered, the number required, the marks for each part and the available time. Copy these into a practice plan before starting a timed attempt.

Use the model paper to learn the format and expected level of response. It is not a leak, a guess paper or a guarantee that those same questions will appear. Retained material remains important even if a particular example does not appear in the model. Where a teacher provides an additional practice paper, compare its scope with this current document first.

## A practical revision cycle for this subject

Begin with one retained unit or manageable group of questions. Read it, close the book and attempt a short recall task. Review the difference between your answer and the required explanation or method. Record the specific weakness, then return to it after a gap. This makes revision measurable without pretending that simply rereading a chapter proves understanding.

Before a timed paper, check your retained-work list for gaps. During the attempt, follow the stated choices and number each answer clearly. Afterwards, separate knowledge errors from presentation or timing errors. Plan the next study block around the weakest category rather than repeating only the questions you already answer comfortably.

Keep notes and past papers useful but subordinate to the current syllabus. An older paper may contain content that is now excluded. Filter such practice deliberately; do not assume an old question is in scope just because it appeared in a board examination before.

## Common questions

### Is this the full textbook or only the subject syllabus?

It is the 11-page Chemistry subject section extracted from the Grade 11 notification booklet. It contains the syllabus notice and accompanying assessment material, not the full textbook. The official multi-subject booklet is available through the source link below.

### Does smart syllabus mean I can skip every chapter mentioned?

No. Read the level of the exclusion: a topic, example, exercise, question or subpart. A chapter can contain both retained and excluded material. The exact table wording matters more than a shortened list shared without its page and exercise references.

### Can I preview the PDF on my phone?

Use Preview document in the attached-document block. If your browser does not display an embedded PDF comfortably, use Open document or Download PDF. Keep the saved copy available for revision, and zoom the original pages when checking small references or Urdu text.

### Does this notice announce my examination date?

A syllabus notification and an examination date sheet are different documents. This booklet concerns scope and assessment guidance for the stated session and annual examination. Check your board's separate date sheet and any later amendments for the examination schedule.

### What if a later notice changes this document?

A later applicable official amendment may change the preparation instructions. Check the issuing authority and your board before the examination, and compare notification dates and reference numbers. If a circulating image differs from the original booklet, use the complete official notice to investigate the difference.
